solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Start zig-zagging around premier university ground and fret about game blockade

indicators.note: around says the two starting letters go either side of the next pair
the starts of the two halves of the hyphenated word zig-zagging, zig and zag, give a letter each
premier means first, so the opening letters of university and ground are taken
about says the synonym for fret is turned round

parts.note: to fret is to worry, or gnaw, at something

explanation.surface: An instruction to zig-zag around a top university's grounds while worrying over a game being blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' works on both halves of the hyphenated zig-zagging, one Z from each; 'around' wraps them round the premier letters; 'about' reverses the synonym for fret.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess term for the position where a player must move and every available move worsens their position, a kind of blockade in the game.

clue.text: Not owing what's excessive

definitions.meaning: a debt not yet payable is not owing
too great, beyond what is warranted

explanation.surface: A debtor's defence that whatever is excessive cannot be owed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both not yet payable, of a debt, and more than is appropriate or warranted.

clue.text: Two African countries twice go and bar awkward actress

indicators.note: twice says the pair of country codes is written two times over

parts.note: Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia and SA is South Africa

indicators.note: awkward says the letters of go and bar are put clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy actress travels around two African countries, visiting each twice and dropping into a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungarian-born Hollywood actress and socialite famous for her many marriages.

clue.text: Hooked on play for the educated involving theologian and I

indicators.note: involving says the word for play wraps around the theologian and I

parts.note: to play a part is to act
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
ED is the standard abbreviation for educated

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on a highbrow play written for the educated, involving a theologian and themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' opens the word for play after its first letter to take the theologian and I; DD (Doctor of Divinity) is the usual crossword theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked on a substance or pastime is dependent on it, which is what being addicted means.

clue.text: Having ensured panto dog was performing, became somewhat cross

indicators.note: the letters are performing, putting on a show in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who checked that the pantomime dog went on stage then got a little annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was performing' signals an anagram of ENSURED PANTO DOG, fifteen letters that rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a dander is a temper, so getting it up means growing angry or irritated.

clue.text: Knowing Kate has diamonds

parts.note: Kate is the title character of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A knowing remark that Kate owns diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate is Katherina, the bad-tempered heroine of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knowing means being astute and sharp in judgement, which is what shrewd describes.

clue.text: The girl having time for one in the Seychelles

indicators.note: in places the time and the one inside the code for the islands

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
an ace counts as one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A girl with time on her hands for one holiday in the Seychelles.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, so it fits the clue's girl as an example of one.

clue.text: Morning run out in the road for disciplinarian

indicators.note: in places the morning and the run out between the letters of the road

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road
AM is the morning, ante meridiem
RO is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A disciplinarian goes out for a morning run along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: RO is how a cricket scorecard records a batter dismissed run out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigidly strict person who enforces discipline, named after the stiff rod once used to load a gun.

clue.text: Spooner says adhesive is to pass down to riverside works

indicators.note: Spooner's swap of the opening sounds of two words, here done by sound

parts.note: mortar is the paste that binds bricks
to will property is to leave it by bequest

explanation.surface: A rule that glue is to be handed down to the factory by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent MORTAR WILL with the opening sounds exchanged becomes WATER MILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill driven by a water wheel stands on a river, so it is a riverside works.

clue.text: One guy with another dependant

parts.note: another guy: Ed is a common man's name
a ward is a dependant in the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: One man keeps company with another who depends on him.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so any single bearer of it is one guy.

clue.text: Drink took two minutes in reaching fellow man

indicators.note: in puts the two minutes between the drink and the word for took

parts.note: tea is a drink
ate means took food
M is the abbreviation for minute, so two of them is MM

explanation.surface: Having a cup of tea took a couple of minutes on the way to meeting a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow member of one's own side in a game or project, a fellow man on the team.

clue.text: Admirable people pitch for baguette

parts.note: a person who is a gem is admirable, so gems are admirable people
the tone of a note is its pitch

explanation.surface: Kind souls set up a stall selling French bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baguette' looks like the loaf, but it is also a cut of precious stone, a narrow rectangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is a long rectangular cut of precious stone, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Surprisingly clean ad for supporter of lamp-stands

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters of clean ad turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: An unexpectedly tidy advertisement for a backer of lamp-stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Branched stands holding several lights; the word is the plural of a Latin singular.

clue.text: Second person is off first? I don't believe it!

indicators.note: first says the word for off leads the phrase

parts.note: gone off is gone away
here is stands for being together with, accompanying
you is the second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A query whether the second person in the queue is leaving first, met with disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as YOU going with AWAY placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disbelief, much like 'get away' or 'go on', telling someone they are kidding.

clue.text: It's a sign to foresters making short films

definitions.note: read as those making short films, a plural noun

parts.note: the V-sign is a hand gesture
loggers fell trees in forests

explanation.surface: A gesture made at woodsmen who are filming short clips.
explanation.definitionFit: People who post short video diaries online, video bloggers, are the ones making short films.

clue.text: Hide alleged responsibility for late morning initially

indicators.note: initially says the late morning comes first in the answer

parts.note: a lie-in is a late morning in bed

indicators.note: alleged means said, so the word for responsibility is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a weight of responsibility is a burden

explanation.surface: Someone hides from blame for a late start in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alleged' gives WAIT, which is said like WEIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurk concealed ready to ambush someone is to hide, so the phrase works as a verb.

clue.text: See 18
No limit to marketability when employed making sweetmeat

indicators.note: no says the letters of limit are taken away from the long word
employed means put to work, so the remaining letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Sales appeal without limits when used to make a confection.
explanation.walkthrough: Take LIMIT from MARKETABILITY to leave ARKETABY; 'when employed' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake baked in a shallow tin and cut into squares, a sweet treat of the sort once called a sweetmeat.

clue.text: Man in Berlin receives degree on Iowa's plant collections

indicators.note: receives says the German man holds the degree inside

parts.note: Herr is German for a man, Mr
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: A German gets a degree on Iowa's plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of dried, pressed plant specimens kept for study, the plural of a Latin word.

clue.text: Animal is 50% anteater and 100% carnivore!

indicators.note: 50% means half, so the first half of the anteater's name is kept

parts.note: the aardvark is an African anteater
the whole of a carnivore: a wolf, a meat-eating predator

explanation.surface: A claim that an animal is half anteater and wholly meat-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: this African animal looks part aardvark and part hyena, and eats termites.
explanation.definitionFit: An African mammal of the hyena family that feeds on termites, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Guard for stripper's lead appearance

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: making an entry is making an appearance

explanation.surface: A doorman on duty for the stripper's headline turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier posted to keep watch is a guard.

clue.text: Not the type of greeting to expect in Tonga?

definitions.text: Not the type of greeting to expect in Tonga?

parts.words: Not the type of greeting to expect in Tonga?
parts.note: Tonga's old name is the Friendly Islands, so a cold welcome there would be unexpected

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders what welcome to expect in a Pacific kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Cook called Tonga the Friendly Islands for the welcome he got.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostile or cold greeting is the opposite of the friendliness Tonga is named for.

clue.text: See 11
Ring shortly to return to Spain

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for shortly reads backwards

parts.note: soon means shortly
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A promise to phone soon on getting back to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of rope with a running knot is a ring of rope.

clue.text: The 3 R's? No ta, a poor reflection on reporter

indicators.note: a poor reflection is a distorted image, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, three letter Rs

explanation.surface: Turning down the three Rs reflects badly on the journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller who reports events to an audience is a reporter of them.

clue.text: See 7
A US city Doctor Who finds haphazardly

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Time Lord drifting aimlessly into New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the TV Time Lord, but it is the anagram signal on WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Done any old how, without method or care, which is what haphazardly describes.

clue.text: Dirty place houses nothing chief exec finds dull

indicators.note: houses says the dirty place contains the next pieces

parts.note: a pigsty is a dirty place
O looks like zero, nothing
DG is director-general, a chief executive

explanation.surface: A boss finds nothing in a grubby office very interesting.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy and uninspired, as stodgy food is, so something dull and tedious.

clue.text: Supposed to have taken liberties

definitions.meaning: to have overstepped, acted too boldly

explanation.surface: Someone was expected to have taken liberties.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both assumed true without proof and having behaved overboldly, taking liberties.
